Markets are trembling amid the latest AI stock sell-off, which has sent shares of major AI players deep into the red. But CNBC's Jim Cramer believes the downturn is not another dot-com crash.

Cramer warned that AI stocks could fall further, particularly semiconductor companies whose shares surged during the AI boom. However, he argued that unlike the speculative businesses that collapsed in 2000, many of today's AI companies are highly profitable.

His biggest concern is smaller AI infrastructure companies such as CoreWeave, Iren and Nebius, which have borrowed heavily to finance data center projects that could face regulatory delays.

Before the election too, Cramer was more careful about tech. On Mad Money, he said the Nasdaq had just closed its worst month since March 2025 and that the week ahead "might be even worse." He said he wanted to see a "crescendo" before putting more money into tech, which he described as stocks getting crushed in the morning and then rallying on big volume to finish higher. He also warned that anti-data center politicians could stop projects if Democrats took control, and data center stocks fell on Wednesday on fears of tighter AI regulation, Reuters reported.

For this article, we scanned Jim Cramer's X feed and watched his latest Mad Money programs on CNBC to pick 10 stocks he sounded positive about. We ranked them in ascending order by the number of hedge fund holders at the end of the second quarter of 2026, according to Insider Monkey's database of 1,006 hedge funds.

#5 GE Vernova Inc. (NYSE:GEV)

Number of Hedge Fund Holders: 106

GE Vernova (NYSE:GEV) makes gas turbines, wind turbines, and equipment for power grids. On X on Oct. 28, Cramer called the stock "an opportunity." In another post that day, he wrote that he was trying "to get into the brains of the GE Vernova sellers," and joked that he was not sure they had any. He sees the selling as a mistake. GE Vernova (NYSE:GEV) is one of the names he is watching closely. Barometer Capital Management pointed to the company's gas turbine and grid backlog in its second-quarter 2026 investor letter. title: AMD Stock Soars After Thursday's Rout. AI Fears Take a Back Seat

This article first appeared on GuruFocus.

Advanced Micro Devices (NASDAQ:AMD) shares surged 12% in Friday trading, recovering ground after Thursday's technology selloff as investors returned to semiconductor stocks. The rebound followed concerns about potential obstacles to AI infrastructure investment that had weighed on chipmakers during the previous session, according to Friday market data.

The earlier retreat came after Democratic candidates secured victories in several midterm election contests, including states with major data center developments. The results raised questions about whether changes in local political priorities could affect the pace of new facility construction and related technology spending.

AMD's recovery came as investors reassessed the potential impact of those developments on the semiconductor industry. Data centers require substantial computing capacity, creating demand for advanced processors used to support artificial intelligence workloads.

However, Friday's rally does not necessarily mean concerns surrounding AI infrastructure expansion have disappeared. Any delays to planned data center projects could influence future spending across the technology supply chain. For AMD, the latest advance reflects renewed buying interest following Thursday's decline, while investors continue to monitor political developments and their potential implications for AI-related demand.

title: NVIDIA and AMD Sell-Off: Which AI Stock Is the Better Buy on the Dip?
detail:
NVIDIA and AMD Sell-Off: Which AI Stock Is the Better Buy on the Dip?
Tirthankar Chakraborty
Fri, November 6, 2026 at 12:00 PM MST 3 min read
^IXIC
NVDA
AMD
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Artificial intelligence (AI) stocks bore the brunt of the market reaction to the U.S. mid-term election results, as concerns over tighter data center regulations and a rise in capital expenditure unnerved investors. The tech-laden Nasdaq, in particular, fell 5.5% on Nov. 5, registering its worst one-day decline since April 2025. A Democratic sweep in Congress fueled fears of stricter restrictions on data center construction, while investors questioned whether massive AI investment could deliver substantial returns.

Leading AI players, including NVIDIA Corporation NVDA and Advanced Micro Devices, Inc. AMD, weren't spared either, with their shares plummeting 9.3% and 17.3%, respectively, yesterday. Despite these short-term market jitters, both NVIDIA and AMD remain well-poised to bounce back, banking on long-term demand for AI chips and data center infrastructure. Therefore, the key question for investors is: with both stocks suffering sharp losses, which one offers the more attractive entry point and is the better buy on the dip? Let's have a look –

Reasons to Be Bullish on NVIDIA

NVIDIA anticipates that its revenue growth momentum will remain strong in the future. The company expects fiscal third-quarter 2027 revenues of $108 billion, plus or minus 2%, according to the company's Aug. 26 press release. That would be more than fiscal second-quarter 2027 revenues of $96 billion, which were up 106% year over year and 18% sequentially.

Revenue growth in the fiscal second quarter was largely driven by its Data Center business, where revenues climbed 117% to $89 billion. Furthermore, NVIDIA's Vera Rubin platform is now in full production, strengthening the company's position to capitalize on rising long-term demand for AI infrastructure and support sustained revenue growth.

Alongside revenue growth, NVIDIA expects its profitability to strengthen. Its gross margin expanded to 75% in the fiscal second quarter, up from 72.4% in the year-ago quarter. The company also reported steady improvements in net income and GAAP operating income, reflecting improving profitability.

Reasons to Be Bullish on AMD

Like NVIDIA, AMD also strengthened its position as a key supplier to AI infrastructure. According to the company's Nov. 3 press release, its fiscal third-quarter 2026 revenues were $13.38 billion, up 45% year over year and 16% sequentially.

Robust demand for Instinct GPUs, EPYC CPUs, and rack-scale AI systems fueled a 97% year-over-year surge in AMD's Data Center revenue to a record $8.5 billion. AMD's profitability improved significantly, with GAAP operating income surging 123% year over year, while non-GAAP earnings per share increased 74% to $2.09.

Bloom Energy Rises 2%, AMD Up 8% as AI Stocks Rebound From Midterm Rout ©@pisitkhambubpha via Canva, @vanitjan via Canva
Key Takeaways

Bloom Energy rose 2% today as AI stocks, AMD among them, bounced back from Thursday's post-midterm selloff.

Bloom had just landed a 900-megawatt NTT DATA deal and a 1-gigawatt plan with California Resources.

Analysts expect Bloom's normalized EPS to climb from $0.76 in 2025 to $8.24 in 2028. Slower US data-center building is the main risk.

Oracle's Dec. 10 report and GE Vernova's turbine orders are the next reads on that demand.

Bloom Energy (BE:NYSE) is up 2% today as AI and data-center stocks bounce back from Thursday's rout after Democrats won control of Congress. Advanced Micro Devices (AMD:NASDAQ) is up 8%.

Bloom fell 16% on Thursday after a week of new demand. It got a 900-megawatt deal with NTT DATA and a plan with California Resources (CRC) for 1 gigawatt or more of fuel cells, on top of its 2.8-gigawatt Oracle (ORCL:NYSE) deal. GE Vernova (GEV:NYSE), which sells turbines into the same buildout, reported third-quarter orders up 96% organically.

The fear is about 2028

UBS analysts estimate construction pauses could put about 30% of the US data-center capacity expected in 2028 at risk. Bloom made 97% of its third-quarter revenue in the US.

AMD fell 17% on Thursday even though its third-quarter revenue rose 45% to $13.4 billion, with data-center sales up 97%, and CEO Lisa Su expects growth "to accelerate further in the fourth quarter."

Bloom's earnings are still headed up

Analysts expect Bloom's normalized EPS to grow more than tenfold from 2025 to 2028:

Bloom Energy (BE): normalized EPS, actual and consensus estimates, $ per share, fiscal 2023-2028 (TIKR)

Yet at Thursday's close Bloom traded at about 40x forward earnings, against a one-year average of 112x.

TIKR tracks 29 analysts on Bloom Energy. How many say "Buy"?

See the full breakdown of Buy, Hold, and Sell ratings on Bloom Energy, along with Wall Street's revenue and earnings estimates, all in one place. More than 500,000 investors use TIKR to research stocks like this one. See Bloom Energy's Analyst Ratings

Oracle is the one to watch

Oracle's free cash flow was negative $5 billion in its quarter ended Aug. 31 as it builds data centers. Its Dec. 10 report will show whether it's sticking with that spending, and the 2.8 gigawatts Bloom is counting on.

GE Vernova's backlog hit $197 billion, and CEO Scott Strazik said on its third-quarter call that it's taking gas turbine reservations for delivery in 2032. Every year a data center waits for a turbine is another year Bloom can pitch power in about 90 days.

California Resources' plan is a non-binding memorandum of understanding that still needs contracts, a final investment decision and EPA permits. Its 2027 budget, out with its fourth-quarter results, will show whether it's funding the project.
